extracted.intended_audience: editors, working journalists, newspaper publishers, complainants, Press Council staff, and auditors
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural criteria used by the Press Council of India to evaluate complaints against the press, and the Council's own accounting and audit policies for its financial statements. Covers journalistic-ethics adjudication criteria (defamation, misleading ads, communal writings, right of reply, suo-motu) and the Council's financial reporting policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right of Reply / Prompt Correction
rubrics_metrics.description: A quick correction is the best remedy. When the person aggrieved sends a contradiction or rejoinder giving his/her side of the case, editors should publish the same with due promptitude and prominence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should not be reluctant to publish contradictions/rejoinders; ignoring the salutary principles of right of reply is an ethical breach that prompts complaints to the Council. Promptness and prominence of correction are emphasised as remedies for inaccurate reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of Complaints Against the Press
rubrics_metrics.description: The Council receives complaints for breaching recognized ethical canons relating to publication or non-publication of news items, statements, cartoons, pictures, photographs, strips, or advertisements in a newspaper, and for professional misconduct by editors, working journalists or staff of newspapers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These categories form the substantive basis for adjudication; the Council builds a code of conduct through adjudications and pronouncements of courts or authorities. Complaints may concern publication or omission across various content forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjudication Outcome Categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard decision categories used in statistical reporting and case disposal: A Upheld; B Dropped; C Assurance/Settled/Amends; D Dropped for Non-pursuance/Sub-judice/Withdrawal/Lack of Substance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These outcome labels are used to classify adjudicated matters and preliminary disposals. Statistics on complaints and adjudications are reported using these four categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defamation — Balance and Caution
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a delicate balance between freedom of speech and protection of reputation; the press must exercise caution and adhere to ethical standards to avoid defaming individuals and to preserve their dignity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alleged defamatory publications are adjudicated by the Council. Remedies/outcomes include upholding complaints, rejecting charges, parties settling or making amends, or dropping where matter becomes sub-judice. The press should take care to avoid unfounded allegations that harm reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suo-motu Cognizance (Regulation 13)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under Regulation 13 of the Press Council Act, 1978, if the Chairperson deems a matter to be of grave significance regarding a breach of journalistic ethics or conduct (any matter falling under Section 14(1)), the Chairperson can take Suo-Motu cognizance; regulations from Regulation 5 onwards will be followed as if it were a complaint made under Regulation 3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Council can initiate inquiries on its own motion for grave ethical breaches; such matters are processed using the same procedural regulations as formal complaints. Statistical reporting records suo-motu adjudications separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition of Communal, Casteist, Anti-National and Anti-Religious Writings
rubrics_metrics.description: The media must not propagate communalism, casteism, social prejudices, or divisive content that disrupts national unity and integration; the media have a role in fostering national unity and curbing divisive forces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such writings are treated as breaches of journalistic ethics; complaints under this category are adjudicated and, where found in breach, are upheld. The Council underscores the press's responsibility to avoid content that promotes division.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misleading Advertisements — Propriety and Detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Newspapers should not publish advertisements which are unlawful or illegal, or contrary to public decency, good taste or to journalistic ethics or propriety. Advertisements must not contain insufficient details that mislead the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commercial advertisements are treated as a form of information and judged by the same ethical standards as editorial content. Complaints alleging misleading ads are adjudicated; findings can result in upheld complaints and requirement of amendment/assurance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles of Journalistic Conduct (General)
rubrics_metrics.description: Through adjudications and guidelines derived from court pronouncements or institutions, the Council has evolved principles of journalistic conduct to help the press uphold faith, respect and dignity while performing duties within ethical boundaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These principles include prompt corrections, right of reply, fair treatment of subjects, avoidance of sensationalism that harms reputation, and adherence to recognized ethical canons. The Council's rulings on cases form case-based guidance for future practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical Accountability of Complaint Handling
rubrics_metrics.description: The Council records and reports numbers of complaints received, pending matters, matters disposed at preliminary stage (settlement/dismissal/lack of substance/non-prosecution/sub-judice) and matters disposed through adjudication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statistical transparency on case volumes and dispositions is part of accountability: e.g., total complaints received, pending carryovers, number adjudicated, number settled preliminarily, and pending at year-end.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accounting Convention — Historical Cost Basis
rubrics_metrics.description: The financial statements are prepared on the basis of historical cost convention unless otherwise stated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the fundamental accounting basis applied to the Council's accounts; unless exceptions are stated, records reflect historical cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method of Accounting — Accrual Basis
rubrics_metrics.description: The Council follows the accrual method of accounting unless otherwise stated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Income and expenses are recognised on accrual basis; exceptions (if any) are to be clearly stated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investments — Classification and Measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: Investments against C.P.F. Fund are classified as earmarked investments; investments against revolving (loans and advances) accounts are treated as current assets. Investments are shown at the principal value increased by interest accrued thereon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Earmarked investments and current investments are presented according to the fund purpose. Measurement includes principal plus accrued interest; additions and maturities are disclosed in schedules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fixed Assets — Valuation and Capitalisation Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Fixed assets are stated at cost of acquisition inclusive of duties and taxes thereon. Other direct expenses related to acquisition are not capitalised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cost of acquisition is capitalised; ancillary/direct expenses not capitalised per policy. Depreciation and disposals are handled as per policy (see Depreciation entry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Depreciation Policy — Income Tax Rates; Disposal Treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Depreciation is charged as per the rates prescribed in the income tax rules. In case of sale of a fixed asset the profit/loss is booked in the year of sale itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depreciation rates follow Income Tax rules; disposals generate immediate recognition of profit/loss in same accounting year. Detailed depreciation schedules accompany the balance sheet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government Grants — Recognition and Transfer Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Government grants are accounted for to the extent of the amount spent. Unspent grant as certified by management is set apart or returned to the government. Grants utilized toward addition of fixed assets are transferred to the Capital Fund. Grants utilized towards interest on C.P.F. Fund are transferred to C.P.F. account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grants are matched to expenditure and treated consistently: spent portion recognised in income/expenditure; utilisation for capital leads to transfer to Capital Fund; earmarked usages are transferred to corresponding funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retirement Benefits — Cash-Basis Treatment and CPF Maintenance
rubrics_metrics.description: Retirement benefits are accounted for on cash basis; hence no provision for gratuity payable, leave encashment etc. is made. The Council maintains its own C.P.F. Fund other than employees who were transferred to NPS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No accrual provision is made for retirement liabilities; payments are recognised when made. The Council operates an internal CPF fund with its own accounting and investments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit and Account Maintenance Requirement (Section 22)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under Section 22 of the Press Council Act, 1978, the accounts of the Press Council of India shall be maintained and audited in such manner as may, in consultation with the Comptroller and Auditor General of India, be prescribed. The Annual Account shall be audited by the appropriate audit party and certified to their satisfaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accounts must be maintained and audited in consultation with the CAG; the Council's accounts are audited by the Audit party of the office of the Director General of Audit, Central Revenues, New Delhi, with certification required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bank Balances, Sundry Debtors, Advances and CPF Reconciliation Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Balances grouped in sundry debtors, advances for books & periodicals, advance to parties, TA advances and loans to staff have not been confirmed/reconciled; balance in C.P.F. Fund and corresponding earmarked investment for C.P.F. is not reconciled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Management opinion states other current assets and advances have realizable value equal to amounts shown, but the schedules note the need for reconciliation and confirmation from parties. Levy fees suspense items must be reconciled with publishers before being taken into income.

rubrics_metrics.name: Levy Fees Suspense and Advance Levy Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Levy Fees Suspense account amounting to an identified sum pertains to levy fees received through NEFT/RTGS/direct deposit where management lacks details to identify payors; amounts are kept in suspense and taken into levy fee only after reconciliation with publishers per policy. Advance levy fees recorded are subject to reconciliation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees deposited but unidentifiable are not recognised as income until reconciled with publishers. Outstanding advance levy fee balances are to be reconciled and adjusted against receipts as per prior-year policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision for Taxation — Exemption Treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: In view of the income of the Council being exempt from tax, no provision for taxation has been made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Council does not provide for tax liabilities given its exempt status; this is disclosed in notes to accounts.
